project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas Vitis-first vine reference module
project_scope.note: Built around leaf-opposed tendrils/inflorescences and berry fruit.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Go to a node and look opposite the leaf: Vitis commonly places a tendril or inflorescence there rather than in the leaf axil.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate and stipulate, often lobed or toothed.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Small and actinomorphic; petals in Vitis may cohere and fall as a cap.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Leaf-opposed tendril/inflorescence is the fast local grape-family cue.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Grapes are easiest when you stop looking at the leaf first and instead check what sits opposite it at the node.

steps.title: 1 · See the grape-vine gestalt
steps.look_for: Woody climbing vine, broad alternate leaves, and grape berries.

steps.title: 2 · Check the node
steps.look_for: A tendril arising opposite the leaf rather than from its axil.
steps.why_it_matters: This is one of the fastest Vitis-versus-Passiflora characters.

steps.title: 3 · Find the tiny flowers
steps.look_for: Small actinomorphic flowers rather than a large showy passionflower.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents vine-family ID from relying only on foliage.

steps.title: 4 · Follow to the berry
steps.look_for: A fleshy berry with several seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Closes the local Vitaceae reproductive pattern.

comparisons.title: Vitaceae vs Passifloraceae
comparisons.rule: Vitis tendrils/inflorescences are commonly leaf-opposed; Passiflora tendrils are axillary and flowers have a corona.

comparisons.title: Vitaceae vs Cucurbitaceae
comparisons.rule: Cucurbits have inferior ovaries and tendrils with different node/flower architecture; Vitis has tiny flowers and berry fruit.

visual_lesson.caveat: Tendril position is more reliable than generic 'vine with lobed leaves.'
